description:
Permanent-kernel tests of `gf2-algebra` return early when feature detection finds no SIMD bundle and are then reported as passed; a kernel test asserts on every host or is not reported as passed.

## Background

The search record `dev/active/1a379447-zen3-cpu-performance/54e70918/survey/simd-early-returns.json`, written by `find-simd-early-returns.py` beside it, states its search rule and lists each test that returns early when a SIMD probe finds nothing, with its package, file and guard. Its `gf2-algebra` rows are the SIMD cross-checks of `crates/gf2-algebra/src/permanent/bipedal3.rs`. Each compares the AVX2 bipedal kernel with a scalar definition and returns at once when the probe reports nothing, so a host without the instruction set reports equivalence that it did not check. libtest has no run-time skip that the test runner reports as skipped. The list-form contract `gf2_kernels_simd::m4rm::contract` always includes the portable reference, refuses an empty implementation list and prints which implementations ran.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each test the search record lists for `gf2-algebra` either runs reference assertions against an independent definition on every host or is not reported as passed when no SIMD implementation is available.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each such test asserts that it exercised a non-zero number of implementations and names them in its output.
- [hard] REQ-03: The regenerated search record lists no `gf2-algebra` test, and the crate's suites pass with and without the `simd` feature on Rust 1.95.

## Notes

Found by the workspace search for SIMD equivalence tests that pass without running. Where a test has nothing to assert without a SIMD implementation, the `gf2-core` tests fail on a stated precondition.
title: Stop gf2-algebra SIMD cross-checks passing without running on hosts without SIMD
